mainTopic: Defects that make a לולב פסול, the source for binding the לולב in the word כפות, and the palms of הר הברזל
overview: This עמוד goes through the physical defects that can make a לולב פסול. It starts at the end of a ברייתא that lists the flaws: thorny, split, curved like a sickle, or hardened. רב פפא explains that 'split' means split like a fork. רבא says a forward curve disqualifies the לולב, but a backward curve is natural and is fine. רב נחמן's ruling on a sideways curve is reported in two versions. רבא adds that a לולב with leaves on only one side is a בעל מום. Next, רב פפא defines the משנה's words נפרצו and נפרדו. He then asks about a split תיומת, which one version of רבי יהושע בן לוי rules is פסול. From the word כפות, the גמרא learns that a לולב should be bound, and it uses this to show that the מצוה is one young לולב, not a hardened branch, the trunk, a thorny branch, two branches, or a single leaf. Finally, אביי rules that palms of הר הברזל are כשר only when their leaves reach one another, and a ברייתא confirms this.

steps.title: The ברייתא lists more defects that disqualify a לולב
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues its list: a thorny, split, or sickle-curved לולב is פסול. A fully hardened לולב is פסול, but one that only looks hardened is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A לולב that is thorny, split, or curved like a sickle is unfit. If it has hardened like wood, it is unfit. If it only looks hardened, it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: We are in the middle of a ברייתא that teaches which physical defects make a לולב פסול. This piece adds thorny, split, curved, and hardened לולבים to the list.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item here is a change in the לולב's natural shape or texture. Notice the fine line at the end: real hardening (חרות) disqualifies, but only looking hardened (דומה לחרות) does not. The rest of this passage will explain and limit these terms one at a time.

keyTerms.meaning: Thorny or prickly. The leaves have become stiff and spiky.
A sickle, the curved blade used for harvesting
Hardened like wood. Some explain it as 'dried and hard'.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the start of the ברייתא. The list began on the previous עמוד, and this passage only picks up its end.

phrases.english: Thorny, split,
curved like a sickle — unfit.
Hardened like wood — unfit.
Merely resembling hardened — fit.

steps.triggerLanguage: קָווּץ, סָדוּק, עָקוֹם דּוֹמֶה לְמַגָּל — פָּסוּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from the previous עמוד, which lists disqualifying defects of a לולב.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A thorny, split, sickle-curved, or truly hardened לולב is פסול. One that only looks hardened is כשר.

steps.title: רב פפא defines a 'split' לולב as one shaped like a fork
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains that the 'split' in the ברייתא means a split so deep that the לולב looks like a two-pronged fork.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: The ברייתא means a לולב that is split so much that it looks like a fork.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains the word סדוק in the ברייתא. Not every small split counts, only one that makes the לולב look like a fork.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Without this explanation, we might think any crack makes a לולב פסול. רב פפא narrows the rule: the two halves must separate so fully that the לולב looks like it has two spines. A smaller split does not fall under this disqualification.

keyTerms.meaning: That it is made or shaped

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
It means where it is shaped like a fork.
phrases.notes: The two halves have fully separated, so it looks like two spines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defines the word סדוק from the ברייתא in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A סדוק לולב is פסול only when the split makes it look like a fork.

steps.title: רבא limits the sickle-curve rule to curving forward
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's phrase 'curved like a sickle' again. רבא says it is פסול only when it curves forward. Curving backward is just how a לולב naturally grows.
steps.simpleTranslation: About 'curved like a sickle,' רבא said: We only said this when it curves forward. But if it curves backward, that is its natural shape.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's phrase again so רבא can limit it. Only a forward curve disqualifies the לולב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason is that a defect means a change from the normal way a לולב grows. A backward curve, toward the spine, is natural (ברייתיה), so it is not a defect. A forward curve, away from the spine, is unnatural, so it makes the לולב פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: We only said this in the case of. This phrase limits an earlier ruling.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up a rule that keeps coming back: if something is the natural way the plant grows, it is not a defect. The next step builds on it.

phrases.english: Curved like a sickle:
phrases.notes: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא again in order to comment on it.

phrases.english: Rava said:
We said this only when it curves forward,
but backward — that is its natural form.

steps.triggerLanguage: עָקוֹם דּוֹמֶה לְמַגָּל, אָמַר רָבָא: לָא אֲמַרַן אֶלָּא לְפָנָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the ברייתא's 'curved' clause from Step 1 and limits it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A forward curve makes a לולב פסול. A backward curve is natural, so the לולב is כשר.

steps.title: רב נחמן on a לולב curved to the side, reported in two versions
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules on a sideways curve. In one version, it is like a forward curve and is פסול. In another version, it is like a backward curve and is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Curving to the sides is like curving forward. Some say he said: It is like curving backward.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן deals with a case רבא left open: a לולב that curves sideways. The גמרא reports two versions of what he said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא gave two choices, forward or backward. A sideways curve falls in between. In the first version, any curve that is not natural disqualifies the לולב. In the second version, only a true forward curve disqualifies it, so the side curve is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: It is like, or it is treated like

steps.confusionAlert: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ does not bring in a new speaker who disagrees. It is a second report of what רב נחמן himself said.

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Curved to the sides — it is like forward (unfit).
And some say: it is like backward (fit).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: לִצְדָדִין — כִּלְפָנָיו דָּמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes רבא's forward/backward split from Step 3 and applies it to a sideways curve.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sideways curve is treated like a forward curve and is פסול. Another version says it is treated like a backward curve and is כשר.

steps.title: רבא: a לולב with leaves on only one side is blemished and unfit
steps.stepSummary: רבא adds a new case. A לולב that grew with leaves on only one side of its spine is a בעל מום and is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: A לולב that grew with only one leaf, meaning leaves on just one side, is blemished and unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new case from רבא. This one is about a לולב that is missing leaves on one side, not about its shape.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now, every defect came from the ברייתא's list. Here רבא adds his own disqualification. He calls this לולב a בעל מום, a blemished thing, because it lacks the normal full form of a לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: One leaf, meaning leaves on only one side of the spine

steps.whatToRemember: A לולב is פסול when it changes from its natural form: split like a fork, curved forward (and maybe sideways), truly hardened, or grown with leaves on only one side. A backward curve is natural and does not disqualify it.

phrases.english: And Rava said:
This lulav that grew with one leaf —
is blemished, and unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הַאי לוּלַבָּא דְּסָלֵיק בְּחַד הוּצָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a new, separate disqualification from רבא, beyond the ברייתא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לולב with leaves on only one side of its spine is a בעל מום and is פסול.

steps.title: רב פפא defines broken-off leaves versus spread leaves
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא explains the משנה's two terms. נפרצו means the leaves broke away from the spine so the לולב looks like a broom, and it is פסול. נפרדו means the leaves are only spread apart, and it is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If its leaves were נפרצו...' רב פפא said: נפרצו means it looks like a broom. נפרדו means the leaves are just spread apart.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. רב פפא then defines its two key words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה ruled נפרצו פסול and נפרדו כשר, but the two words sound alike. רב פפא draws the line between them. If the leaves broke off the spine so the לולב looks like a broom, it is פסול. If the leaves are still attached and just stick outward, it is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: Broken off: the leaves broke away from the spine (פסול)
Spread apart: the leaves are still attached but stick outward (כשר)
'Etc.', meaning the rest of the quote from the משנה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two look-alike words. נִפְרְצוּ (with צ) means broken off and is פסול. נִפְרְדוּ (with ד) means only spread apart and is כשר.

phrases.english: 'If its leaves were broken off,' etc.
Rav Pappa said:
'Broken off' means that it looks like a broom.
'Spread apart' means that the leaves are merely separated.
phrases.notes: The leaves are still attached to the spine and just stick out.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: נִפְרְצוּ — דְּעָבֵיד כִּי חוּפְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the ברייתא's list of flaws to the next line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: נפרצו means the לולב looks like a broom and is פסול. נפרדו means the leaves are only spread apart and it is כשר.

steps.title: רב פפא asks about a split central twin-leaf
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא asks: what is the law if the תיומת, the central double leaf, split into two?
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא asked: if the תיומת split, what is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא asks a new question. This sets up the attempt to answer it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תיומת is the top middle leaf, which is really two leaves fused together. The question is whether splitting it apart counts as a flaw that makes the לולב פסול, even though nothing is missing.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question of law)
The central twin-leaf at the top of the לולב

phrases.english: Rav Pappa asked:
If the central twin-leaf split, what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defining the משנה's terms, רב פפא raises a related case of his own
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a split תיומת makes the לולב פסול

steps.title: Attempted proof from a removed twin-leaf
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings רבי יהושע בן לוי's ruling that a לולב whose תיומת was removed is פסול. It suggests that a split תיומת should be treated the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: (רבי יוחנן) said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that if the תיומת was removed, the לולב is פסול. Doesn't that mean the same is true if it split?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries to answer רב פפא's question with a ruling from רבי יהושע בן לוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע בן לוי only spoke about a removed תיומת. The suggested proof stretches his ruling to cover a split תיומת too, as if both were the same kind of damage.

phrases.english: Come and hear:

phrases.aramaic: דְּאָמַר (רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן) אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: For (Rabbi Yochanan) said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the name רבי יוחנן here, which is why it's in round brackets.

phrases.english: If the central twin-leaf was removed, it is unfit.
Is it not that the same law applies if it split?

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר (רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן) אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers an answer to רב פפא's question
steps.raayaObject: That a split תיומת is פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי יהושע בן לוי: a לולב whose תיומת was removed is פסול

steps.title: Rejection: a removed leaf is different because something is missing
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off. A removed תיומת makes the לולב lacking, but a split one is still all there.
steps.simpleTranslation: No. A removed leaf is different, because the לולב is missing something.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from the last step, so the proof does not settle רב פפא's question. Step 10 brings a second version that answers it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason a removed תיומת is פסול may be that the לולב is incomplete. When the תיומת only splits, nothing is missing, so that reason does not apply. A split תיומת might still be כשר.

phrases.english: No, removed is different,
because it is lacking.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof brought in step 8
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects stretching the ruling about a removed תיומת to a split one
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A removed תיומת is פסול because the לולב is missing a part. A split one is still complete, so the comparison fails.

steps.title: Second version: a split twin-leaf counts as removed
steps.stepSummary: Another version reports that רבי יהושע בן לוי ruled directly about a split תיומת. It is treated as if it were removed, so it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say: (רבי יוחנן) said in the name of רבי יהושע בן לוי that if the תיומת split, it is as if it were removed, and it is פסול.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different report of רבי יהושע בן לוי's words. In this version he answers רב פפא's question directly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version, רבי יהושע בן לוי spoke only about a removed תיומת, so the question stayed open. In this version, he says outright that a split תיומת is just like a removed one. So it is פסול, and the question is answered.

keyTerms.meaning: It becomes like one that was removed

steps.whatToRemember: According to the second version, a split תיומת is פסול, just like a missing one.

phrases.english: Some say:

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר (רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן) אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי:
phrases.english: (Rabbi Yochanan) said that Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
If the central twin-leaf split,
it becomes like one whose twin-leaf was removed, and it is unfit.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי: אָמַר (רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן) אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the same teaching, one that settles רב פפא's question
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A split תיומת is treated like a removed one, so it is פסול
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: In this version, a split תיומת makes the לולב פסול

steps.title: רבי יהודה's source for binding a spread לולב
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, where רבי יהודה says a לולב with spread leaves should be tied at the top. A ברייתא gives רבי טרפון's source: the word כַּפּוֹת (branches) can be read as כְּפוֹת, meaning 'bound.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'רבי יהודה says...' It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי יהודה says in the name of רבי טרפון that the פסוק says 'כפות תמרים.' Read it as 'bound.' If the leaves were spread apart, one should tie them together.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes רבי יהודה's view from the משנה. It then brings a ברייתא that shows where his rule comes from in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the לולב 'כפות תמרים,' palm branches. רבי טרפון reads כפות as 'bound together.' So a לולב should be held tight, and if its leaves spread apart (נפרדו), one should tie them.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Branches of date palms,' the פסוק's name for the לולב

steps.whyThisMatters: This דרשה is the source for the idea that a לולב should be bound together, which ties into the common practice of binding the לולב.

phrases.english: 'Rabbi Yehuda says...'
It was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says in the name of Rabbi Tarfon:
'Branches of date palms': read it as 'bound,'
so if it was spread apart, one should bind it.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר מִשּׁוּם רַבִּי טַרְפוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה's discussion of spread leaves to bring the source for רבי יהודה's view
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the word כפות, a לולב whose leaves spread apart should be tied together

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the hardened palm branch
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי how we know כפות תמרים means the לולב. Maybe it means the old, hardened palm branch.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: How do we know that 'כפות תמרים' means the לולב? Say it means the hardened branch!
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the basic identification of the מצוה. He asks why כפות תמרים must mean the young לולב and not the older, hardened branch of the palm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words כפות תמרים just mean 'palm branches', and a palm tree has many kinds of branches. רבינא wants a reason from the פסוק itself that points to the young לולב specifically.

keyTerms.meaning: Palm branches, the Torah's name for the לולב
An older, hardened palm branch whose leaves stick out and cannot be bound

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
From where do we know that this "branches of date palms"
is referring to the lulav?
Say it means the hardened branch!
phrases.notes: A mature branch whose leaves have hardened and spread outward

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמַּאי דְּהַאי כַּפּוֹת תְּמָרִים דְּלוּלַבָּא הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the reading כפות = 'bound' from step 11 and asks which palm branch the פסוק means.
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that כפות תמרים refers to the young לולב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The words could describe any palm branch, including the hardened one.

steps.title: A hardened branch cannot be bound
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the פסוק requires a branch that is 'bound', and a hardened branch cannot be bound.
steps.simpleTranslation: We need 'bound', and that is not there.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי uses the reading from step 11, that כפות means 'bound', to rule out the hardened branch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The leaves of a hardened branch have already spread out stiffly, so they cannot be held together as one unit. Since the Torah hints that the branch must be 'bound', the hardened branch does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: Bound, held together as one unit

phrases.english: We require "bound," and it is not there.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Any palm branch, even a hardened one, could be meant.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a branch whose leaves can be bound together qualifies, so the hardened branch is excluded.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the palm trunk
steps.stepSummary: If the point is something bound together, maybe the trunk of the palm tree qualifies, since it is always one solid unit.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say it means the trunk!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the answer from step 13. If 'bound' is what matters, the trunk is the most bound part of the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The trunk is completely held together and never spreads apart. So the 'bound' requirement seems to point to the trunk even more than to the לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: The trunk of the palm tree

phrases.english: And say it means the trunk!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'bound' answer of step 13 by pointing to something that is permanently bound.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If being bound is the key feature, the trunk fits best of all.

steps.title: 'Bound' means something that could have spread apart
steps.stepSummary: The word 'bound' only makes sense for something that could have come apart. The trunk is always one solid piece, so it is excluded.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Bound' implies that there is something that can spread apart, and this trunk stays bound forever.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the word 'bound' describes something that is held together even though it could separate. The trunk never separates, so the word does not fit it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You only call something 'bound' if it has parts that could come apart. The young לולב has separate leaves that are held together, which is exactly what the word means. The trunk is just solid wood, so it is not 'bound' at all.

phrases.english: "Bound" implies that there is something that can be spread apart,
and this one stays bound forever.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 14.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Anything that is held together, even the trunk, counts as 'bound'.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'Bound' means separate parts that are held together. The trunk is one solid piece, so it does not qualify.

steps.title: Maybe the verse means the young thorny branch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the כופרא, a young branch that has started to harden but can still be bound with effort.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say it means the כופרא?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers another candidate that seems to fit both rules: its leaves are separate and can still be bound.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The כופרא is not yet fully hardened like the חרותא, and it is not one solid piece like the trunk. So the 'bound' test alone does not rule it out.

keyTerms.meaning: A young palm branch that is starting to harden; its leaves are sharp and thorny

phrases.english: And say it means the kufra (the young, sharp branch)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Proposes a third candidate that passes the 'bound' test from steps 13 and 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the 'bound' test singles out the לולב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The כופרא can also be bound and has separate leaves, so it seems to qualify too.

steps.title: The Torah's ways are pleasant, so no thorny branch
steps.stepSummary: אביי quotes the פסוק 'its ways are ways of pleasantness'. The Torah would not command us to hold a branch that hurts the hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: It is written, 'Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי rules out the כופרא with a general principle: Torah מצוות are pleasant, and holding a thorny branch would hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the answer does not come from the words of the פסוק about the לולב. It comes from a general rule about the Torah's character, taken from משלי. A מצוה that would cause pain does not fit 'ways of pleasantness', so the Torah must mean the soft young לולב.

keyTerms.meaning: Its ways are ways of pleasantness (משלי ג:יז)

steps.whatToRemember: The כפות תמרים of the Torah is the young לולב. The חרותא is too hard to bind, the trunk was never separate, and the כופרא is excluded because of דרכיה דרכי נועם.
steps.whyThisMatters: דרכיה דרכי נועם is used throughout the גמרא as a real halachic principle, not just a nice saying. It can decide how a מצוה is defined.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
"Its ways are ways of pleasantness
and all its paths are peace" is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּרָכֶיהָ דַרְכֵי נוֹעַם וְכׇל נְתִיבוֹתֶיהָ שָׁלוֹם כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 16 and closes the question of which branch is meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The thorny כופרא could be the required branch.
steps.terutzMaskana: The Torah would not command something that hurts, so the soft young לולב is meant.

steps.title: Maybe two palm branches are required
steps.stepSummary: רבא תוספאה points out that כפות is plural, so maybe we must take two palm branches.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא תוספאה said to רבינא: And say it means two palm branches?
steps.whatsHappening: A new question begins. Now that we know which branch is meant, רבא תוספאה asks how many branches we need, since the word sounds plural.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כפות is read in the plural, 'branches'. The smallest plural is two, so the plain reading would seem to require two לולבים.

phrases.english: Rava Tosfa'ah said to Ravina:
And say it means two palm branches?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shifts from which branch is meant to how many branches are needed.
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of taking a single לולב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The plural form כפות suggests at least two branches.

steps.title: The word is spelled without a vav
steps.stepSummary: רבינא answers that in the Torah the word is spelled כפת, with no ו, which points to just one.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'כפת' is written.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא answers from the spelling. Even though we pronounce it as a plural, it is written without the letter ו, like a singular word.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא pays attention both to how a word is read and to how it is written. The missing ו in the written form shows that one branch is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The written spelling without ו, which looks singular

steps.confusionAlert: Do not confuse how the word is read with how it is written. It is read as plural (כפות), but it is written without a ו (כפת), and this answer relies on the written form.

phrases.english: "Kappat" is written.
phrases.notes: Spelled without a ו, so it looks singular

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The plural reading requires two branches.
steps.terutzMaskana: The written spelling without ו shows that only one branch is required.

steps.title: Maybe a single leaf is enough
steps.stepSummary: If the word is singular, maybe one single leaf is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: And say one?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes the singular reading further. Maybe just one leaf is required, not a whole branch.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the spelling shows 'one', we still have to ask: one what? It could mean one single leaf instead of one whole branch.

keyTerms.meaning: One, here meaning a single leaf

phrases.english: And say just one leaf?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of step 19 by taking the singular reading to an extreme.
steps.kashyaTarget: The singular reading from the spelling כפת
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the word is singular, maybe a single leaf is enough.

steps.title: A single leaf is called כף
steps.stepSummary: A single leaf has its own name, כף. Since the Torah wrote כפת, it means one whole branch made of many leaves.
steps.simpleTranslation: That one, a single leaf, is called 'כף'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that if the Torah wanted one leaf, it would have written כף. The form כפת means one branch with many leaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כפת is a middle form. It is written like a singular, which means one branch, but read like a plural, which means many leaves. So the מצוה is one whole לולב, not two branches and not one leaf.
steps.whatToRemember: The written כפת together with the read כפות teaches that we take one לולב (one branch) that has many leaves.

phrases.english: That single leaf is called "kaf."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 20 and settles the number of branches.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise wording, since a different word exists for one leaf
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A single leaf might be enough.
steps.terutzMaskana: A single leaf would be called כף. The Torah's כפת means one whole branch with many leaves.

steps.title: The משנה's ruling on palms from the Iron Mountain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: a לולב from the palms of הר הברזל is כשר.
steps.simpleTranslation: A לולב from the palms of the Iron Mountain is valid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting a new topic by quoting a line from the משנה. This sets up אביי's comment, which comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These palms have only a few leaves along the spine, and the leaves are spaced apart instead of bunched together like a normal לולב. Even so, the משנה rules that such a לולב is כשר.

keyTerms.meaning: The Iron Mountain, a place whose palms have sparse leaves
Valid, fit to use for the מצוה

phrases.english: Palms of the Iron Mountain are valid.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה. These palms have few leaves, spaced far apart.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the discussion of the word כפת ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A לולב from the palms of הר הברזל is כשר.

steps.title: אביי limits the ruling to leaves that overlap
steps.stepSummary: אביי says the משנה only calls it כשר when the top of each leaf reaches the base of the next leaf. If it does not reach, the לולב is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The משנה only taught this when the top of one leaf reaches the base of the next leaf. But if the top of one leaf does not reach the base of the next, it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי adds a condition to the משנה's ruling. The לולב is only כשר if its leaves overlap one another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sounded like a blanket ruling, but אביי narrows it. If the leaves are spaced so far apart that one leaf does not even reach the next, the לולב is פסול. So the ruling of כשר covers only one specific case.

keyTerms.meaning: They only taught this in the case of... (a formula that limits a ruling)
Its base, where it grows out of the spine
Invalid, not fit for the מצוה

steps.confusionAlert: אביי is not disagreeing with the משנה. He is explaining which case the משנה was talking about.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
They only taught this
where the top of this leaf reaches
to the base of that leaf,
phrases.notes: "That leaf" means the next leaf up the spine.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל אֵין רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל זֶה מַגִּיעַ
phrases.english: but if the top of this leaf does not reach
to the base of that leaf, it is invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the משנה's ruling from step 22.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Palms of הר הברזל are כשר only if each leaf reaches the base of the next. Otherwise they are פסול.

steps.title: A ברייתא calls these palms invalid
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to support אביי. The ברייתא says palms of הר הברזל are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: Palms of the Iron Mountain are invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא announces that a ברייתא supports אביי and quotes it. This sets up the next question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says פסול, while our משנה says כשר. The phrase "it was taught this way" tells us the גמרא already sees this ברייתא as support for אביי. The next steps show why.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא (a formula that brings support)

phrases.english: It was also taught this way:
Palms of the Iron Mountain are invalid.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source to back up אביי's distinction from step 23.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's distinction between leaves that overlap and leaves that do not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that says palms of הר הברזל are פסול.

steps.title: The ברייתא seems to clash with the משנה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא points out that our משנה said these palms are כשר, so the ברייתא seems to contradict it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in the משנה that it is valid?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a contradiction between the ברייתא, which says פסול, and our משנה, which says כשר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Two sources give opposite rulings about the same palms. This question is the key to the proof. If the sources are talking about different cases, the clash disappears.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't we learn in our משנה...?

phrases.english: But didn't we learn in the משנה that it is valid?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the ברייתא from step 24 seems to contradict the משנה from step 22.
steps.kashyaTarget: How the ברייתא and the משנה can both be correct.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One source says כשר and the other says פסול about the same palms.

steps.title: Only אביי's distinction fits both sources
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that the משנה and ברייתא are talking about different cases, just as אביי said. This proves אביי right.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this that the law follows אביי. Indeed, learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the contradiction with אביי's distinction and confirms that the ברייתא supports him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה, which says כשר, is talking about leaves that reach one another. The ברייתא, which says פסול, is talking about leaves that do not reach. Because both sources only make sense with אביי's distinction, they prove him right.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it (the point is proven)

steps.whatToRemember: A לולב from the palms of הר הברזל is כשר only if each leaf reaches the base of the next leaf. If the leaves do not reach, it is פסול. The משנה and the ברייתא are both correct, each about a different case.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the practical rule for a לולב with sparse leaves: the leaves must overlap.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it in line with Abaye:
phrases.notes: The only way to fit the two sources together is אביי's distinction.

phrases.english: Indeed, learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the contradiction from step 25 using אביי's distinction.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ברייתא supports אביי. These palms are כשר when the leaves overlap and פסול when they do not.
